slot_note: re-root at stage 1 after architecture 1 (e-bikes by network, the trip record censored by empty docks) was spent at stage 4; about sixty candidates screened on paper and by call-only probes before this draw (design note ## Tried and rejected)
niche: a UK mutual home insurer's reinsurance committee choosing which of four regional home books takes a 2027 catastrophe excess of loss layer (GBP 15 million excess of 10 million each loss occurrence, one reinstatement), valued as the expected 2027 recoveries on its own 2010 to 2025 storm, flood and freeze events brought to the 2027 book less the premium and the expected reinstatement premium, when what a claim costs rises with the claims each repair panel firm has to take on at once and one region's book doubled in 2021 while its panel did not grow
answer: Pennine: the layer is worth about GBP 0.2 million in 2027, against Severn Vale at about GBP -0.4 million, Coastal North at about -0.6 and Fenland at about -0.9 (figures fixed at stage 2)
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every file correctly builds each year's loss occurrences under the hours clause, brings every claim to 2027 by its district's policies against the year's and by the rebuild cost index against its month of loss, and names Severn Vale at about GBP -0.4 million, because no field or document says that what a claim costs depends on how many claims the region's panel firms have to repair at once; the golden prices each event at the repair cost its 2027 scale implies and names Pennine at about GBP 0.2 million.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a catastrophe layer's expected recoveries, which a reinsurance actuary prices from the company's event losses brought to the cover year's exposure and costs; catastrophe modelling knows that claim costs rise with an event's size when local repair capacity is overwhelmed (post-event demand surge), so an event striking a larger book costs more than proportionally more where the repair capacity has not grown.
layer1: event codes only for declared events and missing on late-notified claims; occurrences built from dates of loss under the hours clause, the company choosing each period's start
incurred as paid plus outstanding on 31 October 2026, the 2025 claims still part-reserved
cash settlements carry no panel firm or sign-off date
the 1 January 2021 Calder and Colne book transfer into eight Pennine districts, policies by district and year
storms two days apart (February 2022) that one 72-hour period can hold
attritional windstorm, flood and freeze claims on ordinary days among the event claims
stakeholder_role: the head of reinsurance preparing the committee's placement paper
driver: An event's loss carried to a larger book is scaled claim by claim at the cost each claim carried, when what a claim costs rises with how many claims the region's repair capacity has to take on at once; where the book has grown and the capacity has not, the same event costs more per claim at the forward scale, and only the cost per claim read against claims per unit of capacity across every event shows by how much.
driver_concrete: Each 2010 to 2025 storm, flood and freeze is re-costed as it would strike the 2027 book: its claims scaled by district policies, each claim's cost re-read from the surge curve at the event's 2027 claims per panel firm (Pennine's panel stayed at about 34 firms while its book doubled with the 2021 transfer), and the layer applied to the occurrences the hours clause allows.
stump: A competent analyst brings every claim to 2027 by its district's policies and the rebuild cost index, applies the layer to the occurrences the hours clause allows and names Severn Vale at about GBP -0.4 million, where the golden is Pennine at about GBP 0.2 million; the step that lands it there is pricing a historical event's claims at the cost each claim carried at the event's own scale, when Pennine's pre-2021 events would put about twice as many claims on the same 34 panel firms in 2027.

lineage.niche: which of a bike-share operator's five classic networks gets 300 e-bikes and the net fare revenue a year they add, when the busiest network's stations rarely run dry and the campus network's residence-hall hubs run dry at every teaching-weekday class change, so the rides on record understate the requests
lineage.driver: A launch's added revenue is sized from requests, but the record holds only the requests the service met: where the existing supply runs out at every peak, the unmet requests leave no row, so carrying a pilot's uplift by each candidate's recorded use sends the launch to the candidate whose supply never runs out; only the supply rebuilt second by second from the movements in and out shows which candidate turns away the most requests.
lineage.driver_concrete: Each network's turned-away requests are rebuilt from each station's classic stock (the 03:00 audit, then every undock, dock and van move, second by second) and its requests per stocked second by month, day type and hour, and University, whose residence-hall hubs run dry at every class change, adds the most net fare revenue, while Central, with the most rides on record, rarely runs dry.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst carries the pilot's e-bike share and new-rider uplift to each network's 2025 rides and names Central at about USD 50,000 a year, against University at USD 125,000, whose residence-hall hubs turn away the class-change requests the trip record never shows.
lineage.fate: spent at stage 4 (2026-10-26): both scored readers landed the call (University) by rebuilding the empty-dock seconds; the judge returned SEND_BACK on the grain and the induced riders
